scope: Phone-size fine interlocking crosshatch contrast on opaque jacket and trouser cloth, isolated from source shading and folds
authority: Assistant visual comparison with the owner-supplied S13 photographs; not owner approval of a new swatch, garment or avatar

calibration.previous_material_policy: Retained comparison only. This residual removes the original source low-pass texture and cannot measure all old muddiness; the old material is not forced to fail these bounds.

rejected_initial_projections.reason: Over-strong surface and conspicuous horizontal ribbing at phone size.
Crosshatch too pronounced; the legacy rectangular lapel mapping exposed a false horizontal chest join.
Check groups too large and pronounced at phone size.

calibration.mapping_regression: A smooth vertically constant diagnostic textile must stay continuous across native rows929/930 in unseamed body cloth. The actual legacy rectangular mapping must fail that same one-level rounding bound.

visual_findings: Fine crossed and interlocking yarn detail remains visible without changing the existing dark slate blue-grey color target.
The seam-following S13 mapping removes the invented horizontal upper-chest join from the clearer reconstruction.
The accepted gain keeps the normal-view pattern restrained; registered folds, leg form, seams, buttons and silhouette remain visible.
limitations: The source photographs are not color calibrated and do not establish textile composition.
Residual texture statistics do not replace native/phone visual review or measure every source-pattern defect.
The native renderer hash pins the reviewed pixels; browser/UI and saved-state behavior are verified separately.
